name: Arraigo (Regularization pathways)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires 2 continuous years of presence in Spain (reduced from 3 years by the May 2025 reform), plus either family ties with a legal resident, or an integration-effort report.
This requires demonstrating sufficient economic means.

This requires 2 continuous years of presence in Spain, plus one or more employment contracts guaranteeing at least the SMI (or applicable collective-agreement wage), working at least 20 hours/week. Self-employment does not qualify for this specific route.
This requires being family of a Spaniard, or a parent of a minor Spanish or EU citizen — no minimum unauthorized-presence period applies.
This requires evidencing a prior labour relationship, or labour exploitation, while in an irregular situation.
This requires 2 continuous years of presence in Spain plus a commitment to regulated training for employment.
This requires having previously held a non-exceptional temporary residence status that could not be renewed — explicitly excludes former international-protection (asylum) applicants.

evidence_required.document: Continuous-presence evidence (empadronamiento records, medical/school records, etc.) for the applicable groups
Employment contract meeting the SMI/collective-agreement floor (sociolaboral)
Integration-effort report (social route, if no family ties)

outcome.duration_length: initial authorization 1 year, renewals now 4 years (up from 2 years)
outcome.physical_presence_requirement: the required unauthorized-presence period (2 years for most sub-routes) must be continuous, evidenced through padrón and other documentary records

sources.title: BOE — Real Decreto 1155/2024 (new Reglamento de Extranjería), in force 20 May 2025, Arts. 124 ff.

notes: MAJOR LIVE POLICY EVENT already in force, restructuring the entire category: RD 1155/2024 (in force 20 May 2025) cut the required unauthorized-presence period from 3 years to 2 years for most sub-routes, and reorganized what used to be a simpler binary (arraigo social / arraigo laboral) into SIX distinct sub-routes, one of them (segunda oportunidad) genuinely new. Modeled here as six requirement groups under one route, consistent with the schema's core rule that variation belongs in RequirementGroups — the alternative (six separate route files) would have fragmented what is legally one regularization mechanism with several entry doors. Genuinely important renewal change: renewals extended from 2 to 4 years, a real quality-of-life improvement for arraigo holders reducing how often they must go through the renewal process. UNRESOLVED LEGAL CONFLICT flagged honestly, not silently resolved: whether time spent as an asylum seeker counts toward the 2-year arraigo sociolaboral clock is genuinely disputed — the reglamento itself says no, but some Supreme Court rulings and legal commentary argue it should count in certain circumstances; this file does not take a side, and any real product built on this data should flag it as 'varies by case, consult a lawyer' rather than asserting either position as settled fact. Categorized as 'humanitarian' since arraigo functions as Spain's undocumented-to-documented regularization safety valve, though it isn't asylum/protection in the technical sense — a judgment call flagged the same way as uk_bno and pt_cplp's category placements elsewhere in this dataset.
